items.title: Kerala High Court refuses to stay State's reconstitution of Waqf Board
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has refused to stay the State government's decision to reconstitute the Kerala State Waqf Board by replacing its existing members with nine newly nominated members. [KS Hamza v State of Keralam & ors and connected case] Justice S Manu passed the order at a special sitting held on Saturday, October 17 to consider two petitions challenging the government's October 16 notification nominating new members to the board. The Court examined whether the government had the authority to cancel the appointments of existing Waqf Board members and nominate new members in their place. It also considered whether the government's decision to replace the existing members was consistent with what it had earlier submitted before a division bench about filling only vacancies on the Board. The Court found that the State government had not acted contrary to the earlier Division Bench orders which had permitted the government to take appropriate steps to ensure that the Board was constituted in accordance with law. The two leaders are engaged in a war of words over a purported sting video involving former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. “If my wearing a suit is intolerable to Kumaraswamy, I will get 10 suits stitched and wear them. If my speaking English is intolerable to him, I will continue speaking English,” Kharge said at a press conference in Kalaburagi. He alleged that Kumaraswamy could not tolerate a Dalit making political progress. In the reported sting, Siddaramaiah is linked to alleged blackmail and a purported honey-trap network. items.title: Veeramani POCSO case: Gem Granites manager arrested for helping him evade legal action
items.summary: The Greater Chennai Police (GCP) on Sunday, October 18, arrested Sakthivel, the manager of Gem Granites, for allegedly facilitating financial transactions to help the company’s chairman, R Veeramani, evade legal action in cases involving the alleged sexual abuse of minor girls. The arrest comes amid an ongoing investigation into multiple cases registered against Veeramani under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The police have so far received complaints involving 11 minors and registered seven POCSO cases against him. The latest case was registered on Sunday, based on the statement of another survivor who alleged that she was sexually abused at the residence of Veeramani’s associate Shanthi. According to the police, investigators are examining financial transactions to determine how Veeramani allegedly attempted to evade legal action. As part of the investigation, the police conducted searches at Veeramani’s residence on Lloyds Road in Chennai, his farmhouse in Kanathur, and the office of Chamundeshwari Natural Stone. items.title: YSRCP withdraws from Punganur municipality polls, alleges TDP violence
items.summary: The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) will not contest the Punganur municipality elections in Andhra Pradesh, citing violence and intimidation by the ruling party. The party said inadequate police security arrangements prevented its candidates from filing nominations before the deadline. Peddireddi Ramachandra Reddy, the party’s MLA from Punganur, announced the decision at a meeting with supporters at his residence in Tirupati on Sunday, October 18. He said YSRCP candidates could not submit their papers without a “free and fair atmosphere” and alleged that rival party workers had used violence while security for his party’s candidates was inadequate. The party failed to file any nominations in Punganur before the 3 pm deadline. YSRCP president and former Chief Minister YS Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the ruling coalition of using intimidation, violence and state machinery to obstruct Opposition candidates. He alleged that police and election officials had not acted impartially. Punganur witnessed violent clashes between the YSRCP and Telugu Desam Party (TDP) members during the nomination process, in which YSRCP MP Midhun Reddy’s convoy was attacked allegedly by TDP cadres. items.title: Why gig workers can’t choose working hours even in extreme weather
items.summary: Even as gig and platform workers form the backbone of several companies that control their incentives, pay and working hours, companies do not have to comply with labour standards for workers’ occupational health, safety or working conditions under India’s labour codes. This makes gig workers more susceptible to extreme climate events, our reporting found. The Code on Social Security defines and includes gig workers, but its implementation is unclear, and the lack of mention of gig workers in the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code (OSH, 2020), puts them at risk of climate impacts on health, productivity and earnings. This is the fourth part of our series on how India’s new labour codes have a climate blindspot, which particularly impacts women workers. You can read the first three parts here , here and here . Ganga (name changed), a 43-year-old gig worker based in Faridabad, is a “partner” with Urban Company. She was first drawn to gig work about a decade ago due to its flexibility of working hours and a decent income. But now, the nature of work has changed.
